identity.name: Rosa Guerrero
identity.work: small-business owner (a party-supply and rental shop)
identity.language: heavy code-switching (ES/EN), slides between the two mid-thought

birth.tz_expect: America/Puerto_Rico (UTC-4, no DST ever) — time is approximate: 'around 2pm, my mother says'

arrived.presenting: runs everyone's life but her own; exhausted, can't ask for help, feels like she's disappearing behind the counter
arrived.in_her_words: Todo el mundo me llama cuando algo se rompe, pero when I need something? I just… figure it out sola. Siempre sola.

beliefs: asking for help means I'm a burden
if I stop holding everything, todo se cae
protections: being the strong one for everybody
patterns: takes on other people's crises to avoid her own
resources: her sister in Bayamón, who calls every Sunday
her hands — she can fix or build anything
the shop's regulars who treat her like familia
psyche.origin: the oldest of six; mother worked nights, so Rosa raised the little ones — needing was a luxury the household couldn't afford

unaware_of: asking for help means I'm a burden

beats.note: arrives insisting she only needs 'un poco de organización'; deflects every question back to her family
code-switches into Spanish describing her mother's night shifts — first crack: 'yo era la mamá chiquita'
lets an employee cover a weekend; texts her sister instead of white-knuckling it alone
names it: 'pedir ayuda no me hace débil' — I-must-not-need starting to loosen
still catches herself saying 'estoy bien' automatically, but now she notices and laughs

voice: warm, fast, maternal; slides between Spanish and English inside a single sentence — English for the practical, Spanish for the tender and the true; jokes to soften a hard admission, then says it anyway
